findings.note: The .shellcheckrc rationale is factually wrong about the sites it suppresses. It states 'Every hit is a backtick inside a single-quoted literal: a Markdown code span being grepped for in a review log ... or a sed script matching one'. Running shellcheck --norc over the suite gives 16 SC2016 hits, and at least two are not that case: tests/go/test-fsm.sh:186 is sed 's/effort: \$REV_EFFORT/effort: high/' with no backtick anywhere on the line, and tests/manifest/test-manifests.sh:7 is a node -e '...' script whose trigger is the JavaScript template placeholder ${required} at line 60. Since this comment is the sole justification for a repo-wide disable rather than per-line 'shellcheck disable=SC2016' directives, a maintainer reading it would not expect $VAR-shaped literals to be unchecked repo-wide. Either widen the comment to cover escaped shell-variable names in sed scripts and JS template literals, or scope the disable to the sites that need it.

activeExisting was widened from an allowlist to a denylist: 'record.Status == "open"' became 'record.Status != "fixed"'. Today the written vocabulary is exactly open/fixed/override-pending/overridden/superseded, so the behaviour is right, but any row with an empty or unrecognised status now suppresses creation of a matching current finding, which would drop a live blocker out of Result.Findings and OpenFindings with no trace. An allowlist (Blocks(status) || StatusOverridden || StatusSuperseded) keeps the same behaviour without the open-ended failure mode, and would not silently absorb a future status such as a withdrawal.

The 11-line comment above the fix transition claims a pending override that was actually fixed 'had no way out' and that this closes it. The transition it guards still requires previousRuns[record.RunID] || resetFinding(...), so an unchained run (no --previous-run, no reset) leaves the override-pending row untouched and 'override list --pending' still exits 1. The fix is real but conditional; the comment reads as unconditional. Worth one clause saying the run must be chained to the run that recorded it.

readJSONL is now a near-exact copy of the generic reader it could call. internal/findings/findings.go:475-502 and internal/state/state.go:53-79 have the same open/NotExist branch, the same deferred close-with-discarded-error, the same scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), maxJSONLLineBytes+2) line, the same trim/skip-blank/unmarshal loop and the same 'return records, scanner.Err()'. The only difference is []Record{} versus nil on a missing file. maxJSONLLineBytes = 1 << 20 is now declared four times (findings.go:19, state.go:21, runchain.go:17, reviewlog.go:21) with a comment that only findings.go carries in full. state.ReadJSONL[Record] plus one shared constant would remove three copies and keep the CRLF rationale in a single place.

Cross-shard: the +2 rationale this shard documents is not applied to the fifth JSONL reader added by the same branch. internal/fsm/record/record.go:156 does sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 1<<20), 1<<20) with maxTokenSize exactly 1<<20 and no +2, which is precisely the case findings.go:15-18 explains bufio rejects (bufio needs the line terminator to fit alongside the token). A run audit line of exactly 1 MiB is readable by findings/state/runchain/reviewlog and rejected by the record layer. Raise it to 1<<20 + 2, or better, share the constant.

findings.PendingOverrides has no production caller. The CLI re-implements the same pending filter inline over ListOverrides in cmd/metareview/main.go:513-530 (count pending, print, exit 1). The helper carries the CI contract in its doc comment ('CI should refuse to pass while this is non-empty') while the code that actually enforces it lives elsewhere, so the two can drift. Either have handleOverride call PendingOverrides or delete it.
